compare_blocks.body:
Align the conditions first: the same acceptance meeting, the same three notes, half a day left in both cases. compare_blocks.title: One-minute comparison

compare_blocks.body:
In a fictional client review, two people receive the same reports. Either can acknowledge how the fault affects the client and record exactly what happened during a test. Those tasks do not distinguish ENFJ from ESFP.

Both types share preferences for directing attention outward (E) and weighing people and values in decisions (F). Their roles and responsibilities still shape what they do in a meeting.

The difference sits on two axes: material (S/N) and outward stance (J/P). The first says which kind of information gets trusted; the second says whether things get settled outward or left open. One acceptance meeting spreads both out.

### ENFJ and ESFP: three fix requests, two answers to "what counts as clear"

In a fictional acceptance review, the client reports slow login, a crowded report layout and intermittent export failures. Both reviewers see the same notes and authorized test results. One looks for a pattern across the reports. Another checks the observed delay, the affected column and the recorded failures. Either reviewer can do both.

The observations show what happened in the tests. Patterns across reports can suggest which explanations are worth investigating. Neither the choice of notes nor the order of the checks can establish a personality type.

Conditions rewrite the approach. When the contract names the acceptance items, both check them item by item first; when the fault is intermittent and the logs unobtainable, both merging and reproduction rest on guesswork and both turn to asking what the client actually said; with twenty minutes and a required answer, both may say the fault will be reproduced this afternoon and a plan delivered tomorrow. Conversely, if the client says they will not sign until the first item is solved, both may push the other two back.

So the difference is not in how much either cares, and not in who is more professional, but in which kind of evidence each trusts to support the next step.

### ENFJ and ESFP: why Ni and Se are shared while the judging seats change

In the four-function notation used here, ENFJ is Fe–Ni–Se–Ti and ESFP is Se–Fi–Te–Ni. The names that overlap are the two perceiving processes: Ni second in ENFJ and fourth in ESFP, Se third in ENFJ and first in ESFP — seats offset, not pairwise exchanged. The judging seats change within the same family's attitudes: Fe against Fi, Ti against Te.

Both types are extraverted, so type dynamics places the outward-facing process first. ENFJ’s J points to a judging process, Fe. ESFP’s P points to a perceiving process, Se. Both have Feeling in their four-letter code, but ESFP’s preferred judging process is the inward-facing auxiliary Fi.

compare_blocks.title: Why they are easily confused

compare_blocks.body:
When delivering together, splitting the two threads usually saves effort: one turns notes into checkable phenomena, the other negotiates those phenomena into an order the client can accept. Who takes which follows familiarity with the product, responsibility for client communication, current workload and past work samples — not type; either type can do both segments.

### ENFJ and ESFP: an acceptance meeting with three client fix requests

(Fictional scene) A store point-of-sale system goes live for acceptance. The client sends the store manager and the regional manager, the contract states the balance is paid after acceptance, and the delivery side has half a day.

In this fictional review, both reviewers receive the same account from the store manager and regional manager, plus the same test record. Either can check which problems block opening or reporting, notice a pattern across the reports, and then decide which follow-up choices can be settled.

Passing acceptance depends on the agreed criteria and evidence. Either reviewer can document what has been observed and discuss priorities with the client. Avoid committing to a cause that the test record has not confirmed.

When checking, sort the material into five kinds first: the client's own words, the contract and acceptance requirements, phenomena already reproduced, questions still open, and hypotheses about cause. Items can be traced to a contract clause, a quotation or a ticket — they do not all have to rest on one reproduction, since intermittent faults, explicit aesthetic requests and contract-named acceptance items need not be reproducible on the spot. Comparing the reasons behind each person's ordering afterwards is more useful than counting how many items overlap: reasons centred on phenomena and reproduction conditions, and reasons centred on commitments and relationships, usually sit in different places. That is for agreeing who takes which segment next time, not for typing.

Keep the counterexamples: asked for written material, an ESFP can also produce a categorised list; with the client standing alongside, an ENFJ can also tap through the product personally.

### ENFJ and ESFP: the projector and the network fail on demo day

(Fictional scene) The client's meeting-room projector will not recognise the laptop, the Wi-Fi wants a verification code, and the demo starts in ten minutes.

In this fictional scene, one approach handles the people: announce a five-minute delay, ask the contact to fetch the code, and switch the content to a spoken version that needs no projector. The other handles the equipment: change the adapter, try another machine, tether from a phone, and keep the people nearby talking while doing it. Either type can combine both; which step gets taken depends on the division of work, authority and the information at hand.

Which is easier depends on whether the fault can be solved in ten minutes, and on whether this demo is about the equipment or the content: if it can be solved, acting first saves the cost of changing the agenda; if it cannot, settling the people first preserves the meeting itself. A counterexample: with senior client staff present, an ESFP may also ask for a ten-minute delay; with equipment that is clearly repairable, an ENFJ may also crouch down and fix it. Anything involving mains power, working at height or dismantling venue equipment follows site rules and the venue operator's instructions, and is not attempted independently.

### ENFJ and ESFP: a friend's trip, half a day of childcare

In a fictional afternoon of childcare, two adults know the same caregiver instructions and meal and rest times. One prefers to agree on a tentative order for the afternoon. Another keeps the choice of activity open within those constraints. Either can change plans if the child needs a break.

The example illustrates J/P, the preference for making an outward arrangement or keeping options open. Both adults can observe what interests the child and follow the caregiver’s instructions. The choice of schedule does not measure how well either cares for the child.

Afterwards, record what is visible: when he laughed, when he started watching the door, whether he was hungry or tired, who was present, what time it was, whether a stranger was there. None of these details alone shows how well the half day went, and none can be read backwards into an adult's type; a child who cannot explain is normal, and asking whether he wants to come back tomorrow is more useful than concluding for him.
compare_blocks.title: Illustrative scenarios

compare_blocks.body:
The first reads ESFP as only good for atmosphere. Their reproduction notes at an acceptance meeting may be more detailed than anyone's, coming from a work habit of not trusting what has not been seen, or from the requirements of the post — neither is evidence of type.

The second reads ENFJ as only good at relationships. Their memory for delivery milestones is often accurate to half a day, perhaps because the milestone sits in the contract and has to be accounted for to someone — that is duty and experience, not proof of four letters.

The third turns S/N into a question of who is more far-sighted. Talking about maintenance in three months or about opening the doors tomorrow morning depends on the contract and the client structure; N means connections and possibility get taken more often, not a higher vantage point, and S means fact and experience get taken more often, not short sight.

The fourth uses who moves first as a test. What gets done first depends on role, experience, deadline and conditions on site; the same person changes order in a different meeting, and order itself has no classificatory value.

Not a division by type; either can complete the whole process.

Taking the same fictional note sheet and writing a reproduction record and a fix schedule separately is a way to feel the difference between the two tasks, not to judge who is competent.
faq_blocks.question: Which is better suited to acceptance delivery or customer success?

faq_blocks.answer:
Usually on what the client is actually unhappy about: one records the phenomenon, the other records the attitude, and afterwards they do not match.

body: In a fictional client review, two people receive the same reports. Either can acknowledge how the fault affects the client and record exactly what happened during a test. Those tasks do not distinguish ENFJ from ESFP.
Both types share preferences for directing attention outward (E) and weighing people and values in decisions (F). Their roles and responsibilities still shape what they do in a meeting.

The difference sits on two axes: material (S/N) and outward stance (J/P). The first says which kind of information gets trusted; the second says whether things get settled outward or left open. One acceptance meeting spreads both out.
### ENFJ and ESFP: three fix requests, two answers to "what counts as clear"

In a fictional acceptance review, the client reports slow login, a crowded report layout and intermittent export failures. Both reviewers see the same notes and authorized test results. One looks for a pattern across the reports. Another checks the observed delay, the affected column and the recorded failures. Either reviewer can do both.

The observations show what happened in the tests. Patterns across reports can suggest which explanations are worth investigating. Neither the choice of notes nor the order of the checks can establish a personality type.

Conditions rewrite the approach. When the contract names the acceptance items, both check them item by item first; when the fault is intermittent and the logs unobtainable, both merging and reproduction rest on guesswork and both turn to asking what the client actually said; with twenty minutes and a required answer, both may say the fault will be reproduced this afternoon and a plan delivered tomorrow. Conversely, if the client says they will not sign until the first item is solved, both may push the other two back.
So the difference is not in how much either cares, and not in who is more professional, but in which kind of evidence each trusts to support the next step.
### ENFJ and ESFP: why Ni and Se are shared while the judging seats change

In the four-function notation used here, ENFJ is Fe–Ni–Se–Ti and ESFP is Se–Fi–Te–Ni. The names that overlap are the two perceiving processes: Ni second in ENFJ and fourth in ESFP, Se third in ENFJ and first in ESFP — seats offset, not pairwise exchanged. The judging seats change within the same family's attitudes: Fe against Fi, Ti against Te.

Both types are extraverted, so type dynamics places the outward-facing process first. ENFJ’s J points to a judging process, Fe. ESFP’s P points to a perceiving process, Se. Both have Feeling in their four-letter code, but ESFP’s preferred judging process is the inward-facing auxiliary Fi.

Fe and Se describe different dominant processes in the model. They do not predict who speaks or acts first. Sources vary in how they label the third process. Compare the [ENFJ profile](/en/personality/enfj) and the [ESFP profile](/en/personality/esfp) for the individual preferences.

body: Align the conditions first: the same acceptance meeting, the same three notes, half a day left in both cases. If one is the project manager and the other drafted in to help, or one already has two projects on their desk, duty and load will swamp both columns. Both types can use the other's approach; the rows only state which kind of evidence tends to be taken first.

| The same acceptance meeting (same notes, half a day left) | ENFJ: evidence likely to be attended to first | ESFP: evidence likely to be attended to first | What this row illustrates |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| How the three notes get consolidated | Whether the same reports point to a common pattern or underlying cause | Whether each can be reproduced on the spot, and when and how often it appears | What counts as material, leaning S/N |
| Both review the same reports before setting a priority | Look for a link between failures and consider what could happen if the pattern continues | Check which failures were observed and at what stage they blocked the work | Information gathering: S/N |
| How the fix list is ordered | May set a provisional order for the same fixes and revise it as needed | May keep feasible orders open while the same reproduction checks finish | Outward stance, leaning J/P |

sections.title: ENFJ and ESFP in one minute

body: When delivering together, splitting the two threads usually saves effort: one turns notes into checkable phenomena, the other negotiates those phenomena into an order the client can accept. Who takes which follows familiarity with the product, responsibility for client communication, current workload and past work samples — not type; either type can do both segments.
### ENFJ and ESFP: an acceptance meeting with three client fix requests

(Fictional scene) A store point-of-sale system goes live for acceptance. The client sends the store manager and the regional manager, the contract states the balance is paid after acceptance, and the delivery side has half a day.

In this fictional review, both reviewers receive the same account from the store manager and regional manager, plus the same test record. Either can check which problems block opening or reporting, notice a pattern across the reports, and then decide which follow-up choices can be settled.

Passing acceptance depends on the agreed criteria and evidence. Either reviewer can document what has been observed and discuss priorities with the client. Avoid committing to a cause that the test record has not confirmed.

When checking, sort the material into five kinds first: the client's own words, the contract and acceptance requirements, phenomena already reproduced, questions still open, and hypotheses about cause. Items can be traced to a contract clause, a quotation or a ticket — they do not all have to rest on one reproduction, since intermittent faults, explicit aesthetic requests and contract-named acceptance items need not be reproducible on the spot. Comparing the reasons behind each person's ordering afterwards is more useful than counting how many items overlap: reasons centred on phenomena and reproduction conditions, and reasons centred on commitments and relationships, usually sit in different places. That is for agreeing who takes which segment next time, not for typing.
Keep the counterexamples: asked for written material, an ESFP can also produce a categorised list; with the client standing alongside, an ENFJ can also tap through the product personally.
### ENFJ and ESFP: the projector and the network fail on demo day
(Fictional scene) The client's meeting-room projector will not recognise the laptop, the Wi-Fi wants a verification code, and the demo starts in ten minutes.

In this fictional scene, one approach handles the people: announce a five-minute delay, ask the contact to fetch the code, and switch the content to a spoken version that needs no projector. The other handles the equipment: change the adapter, try another machine, tether from a phone, and keep the people nearby talking while doing it. Either type can combine both; which step gets taken depends on the division of work, authority and the information at hand.

Which is easier depends on whether the fault can be solved in ten minutes, and on whether this demo is about the equipment or the content: if it can be solved, acting first saves the cost of changing the agenda; if it cannot, settling the people first preserves the meeting itself. A counterexample: with senior client staff present, an ESFP may also ask for a ten-minute delay; with equipment that is clearly repairable, an ENFJ may also crouch down and fix it. Anything involving mains power, working at height or dismantling venue equipment follows site rules and the venue operator's instructions, and is not attempted independently.
### ENFJ and ESFP: a friend's trip, half a day of childcare

In a fictional afternoon of childcare, two adults know the same caregiver instructions and meal and rest times. One prefers to agree on a tentative order for the afternoon. Another keeps the choice of activity open within those constraints. Either can change plans if the child needs a break.

The example illustrates J/P, the preference for making an outward arrangement or keeping options open. Both adults can observe what interests the child and follow the caregiver’s instructions. The choice of schedule does not measure how well either cares for the child.

Afterwards, record what is visible: when he laughed, when he started watching the door, whether he was hungry or tired, who was present, what time it was, whether a stranger was there. None of these details alone shows how well the half day went, and none can be read backwards into an adult's type; a child who cannot explain is normal, and asking whether he wants to come back tomorrow is more useful than concluding for him.
sections.title: ENFJ and ESFP at work and in relationships

body: The first reads ESFP as only good for atmosphere. Their reproduction notes at an acceptance meeting may be more detailed than anyone's, coming from a work habit of not trusting what has not been seen, or from the requirements of the post — neither is evidence of type.

The second reads ENFJ as only good at relationships. Their memory for delivery milestones is often accurate to half a day, perhaps because the milestone sits in the contract and has to be accounted for to someone — that is duty and experience, not proof of four letters.

The third turns S/N into a question of who is more far-sighted. Talking about maintenance in three months or about opening the doors tomorrow morning depends on the contract and the client structure; N means connections and possibility get taken more often, not a higher vantage point, and S means fact and experience get taken more often, not short sight.

The fourth uses who moves first as a test. What gets done first depends on role, experience, deadline and conditions on site; the same person changes order in a different meeting, and order itself has no classificatory value.

body: When two results differ, check the item bank's name, version, language and scoring definition first, then whether you were referring to the acceptance meeting or the retrospective report. The post reshapes behaviour: people who mainly maintain systems consolidate first more often, people who mainly work on site reproduce first more often. Worth noting, but not readable backwards into a type.

Put the practice in everyday scenes with a similar role: take three notes you received recently and write four lines for each — what your role was, how tight the deadline was, what material you had (quotations, clauses, reproduction records, logs), and why you took that kind first. Afterwards read the recurring reason across the four lines rather than counting how many times you consolidated or reproduced. These notes serve reflection, are not scored, do not assign a type, and a few weeks of trend cannot replace the interpretation of an assessment result.

So the difference is not in how much either cares, and not in who is more professional, but in which kind of evidence each trusts to support the next step.

### ENFJ and ESFP: why Ni and Se are shared while the judging seats change

In the four-function notation used here, ENFJ is Fe–Ni–Se–Ti and ESFP is Se–Fi–Te–Ni. The names that overlap are the two perceiving processes: Ni second in ENFJ and fourth in ESFP, Se third in ENFJ and first in ESFP — seats offset, not pairwise exchanged. The judging seats change within the same family's attitudes: Fe against Fi, Ti against Te.

Both types are extraverted, so type dynamics places the outward-facing process first. ENFJ’s J points to a judging process, Fe. ESFP’s P points to a perceiving process, Se. Both have Feeling in their four-letter code, but ESFP’s preferred judging process is the inward-facing auxiliary Fi.

Fe and Se describe different dominant processes in the model. They do not predict who speaks or acts first. Sources vary in how they label the third process. Compare the [ENFJ profile](/en/personality/enfj) and the [ESFP profile](/en/personality/esfp) for the individual preferences.

sections.body_md:
Align the conditions first: the same acceptance meeting, the same three notes, half a day left in both cases. If one is the project manager and the other drafted in to help, or one already has two projects on their desk, duty and load will swamp both columns. Both types can use the other's approach; the rows only state which kind of evidence tends to be taken first.

| The same acceptance meeting (same notes, half a day left) | ENFJ: evidence likely to be attended to first | ESFP: evidence likely to be attended to first | What this row illustrates |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| How the three notes get consolidated | Whether the same reports point to a common pattern or underlying cause | Whether each can be reproduced on the spot, and when and how often it appears | What counts as material, leaning S/N |
| Both review the same reports before setting a priority | Look for a link between failures and consider what could happen if the pattern continues | Check which failures were observed and at what stage they blocked the work | Information gathering: S/N |
| How the fix list is ordered | May set a provisional order for the same fixes and revise it as needed | May keep feasible orders open while the same reproduction checks finish | Outward stance, leaning J/P |
| Both have thirty minutes and the same checks remain open | Agree on a provisional follow-up order and a time to revisit it | Keep two workable follow-up orders open until the same checks finish | Approach to outward arrangements: J/P |
| What each prepares beforehand | What connections across the existing reports might explain other similar failures | What the shared test record says about the device, steps and observed failure | What counts as material, leaning S/N |
| How detailed the minutes get | Agree on a provisional follow-up plan, with the same observations recorded | Keep follow-up options open while the same observations are being explained | Outward stance, leaning J/P |

None of these rows is a scale of ability. Someone with years in customer success will usually ask who will read the minutes, whatever their type; someone handling acceptance independently for the first time may only want to record every symptom. As for whether to calm a client first or state the facts first, that is a difference of landing point inside the shared F, and this page neither turns it into a separate axis nor recommends it for typing.
sections.title: ENFJ and ESFP in one minute

sections.body_md:
When delivering together, splitting the two threads usually saves effort: one turns notes into checkable phenomena, the other negotiates those phenomena into an order the client can accept. Who takes which follows familiarity with the product, responsibility for client communication, current workload and past work samples — not type; either type can do both segments.

### ENFJ and ESFP: an acceptance meeting with three client fix requests

(Fictional scene) A store point-of-sale system goes live for acceptance. The client sends the store manager and the regional manager, the contract states the balance is paid after acceptance, and the delivery side has half a day.

In this fictional review, both reviewers receive the same account from the store manager and regional manager, plus the same test record. Either can check which problems block opening or reporting, notice a pattern across the reports, and then decide which follow-up choices can be settled.

Passing acceptance depends on the agreed criteria and evidence. Either reviewer can document what has been observed and discuss priorities with the client. Avoid committing to a cause that the test record has not confirmed.

When checking, sort the material into five kinds first: the client's own words, the contract and acceptance requirements, phenomena already reproduced, questions still open, and hypotheses about cause. Items can be traced to a contract clause, a quotation or a ticket — they do not all have to rest on one reproduction, since intermittent faults, explicit aesthetic requests and contract-named acceptance items need not be reproducible on the spot. Comparing the reasons behind each person's ordering afterwards is more useful than counting how many items overlap: reasons centred on phenomena and reproduction conditions, and reasons centred on commitments and relationships, usually sit in different places. That is for agreeing who takes which segment next time, not for typing.

Keep the counterexamples: asked for written material, an ESFP can also produce a categorised list; with the client standing alongside, an ENFJ can also tap through the product personally.

### ENFJ and ESFP: the projector and the network fail on demo day

(Fictional scene) The client's meeting-room projector will not recognise the laptop, the Wi-Fi wants a verification code, and the demo starts in ten minutes.

In this fictional scene, one approach handles the people: announce a five-minute delay, ask the contact to fetch the code, and switch the content to a spoken version that needs no projector. The other handles the equipment: change the adapter, try another machine, tether from a phone, and keep the people nearby talking while doing it. Either type can combine both; which step gets taken depends on the division of work, authority and the information at hand.

Which is easier depends on whether the fault can be solved in ten minutes, and on whether this demo is about the equipment or the content: if it can be solved, acting first saves the cost of changing the agenda; if it cannot, settling the people first preserves the meeting itself. A counterexample: with senior client staff present, an ESFP may also ask for a ten-minute delay; with equipment that is clearly repairable, an ENFJ may also crouch down and fix it. Anything involving mains power, working at height or dismantling venue equipment follows site rules and the venue operator's instructions, and is not attempted independently.

### ENFJ and ESFP: a friend's trip, half a day of childcare

In a fictional afternoon of childcare, two adults know the same caregiver instructions and meal and rest times. One prefers to agree on a tentative order for the afternoon. Another keeps the choice of activity open within those constraints. Either can change plans if the child needs a break.

The example illustrates J/P, the preference for making an outward arrangement or keeping options open. Both adults can observe what interests the child and follow the caregiver’s instructions. The choice of schedule does not measure how well either cares for the child.

Afterwards, record what is visible: when he laughed, when he started watching the door, whether he was hungry or tired, who was present, what time it was, whether a stranger was there. None of these details alone shows how well the half day went, and none can be read backwards into an adult's type; a child who cannot explain is normal, and asking whether he wants to come back tomorrow is more useful than concluding for him.
sections.title: ENFJ and ESFP at work and in relationships

sections.body_md:
The first reads ESFP as only good for atmosphere. Their reproduction notes at an acceptance meeting may be more detailed than anyone's, coming from a work habit of not trusting what has not been seen, or from the requirements of the post — neither is evidence of type.

The second reads ENFJ as only good at relationships. Their memory for delivery milestones is often accurate to half a day, perhaps because the milestone sits in the contract and has to be accounted for to someone — that is duty and experience, not proof of four letters.

The third turns S/N into a question of who is more far-sighted. Talking about maintenance in three months or about opening the doors tomorrow morning depends on the contract and the client structure; N means connections and possibility get taken more often, not a higher vantage point, and S means fact and experience get taken more often, not short sight.

The fourth uses who moves first as a test. What gets done first depends on role, experience, deadline and conditions on site; the same person changes order in a different meeting, and order itself has no classificatory value.
sections.title: ENFJ and ESFP: avoiding misreads

sections.body_md:
When two results differ, check the item bank's name, version, language and scoring definition first, then whether you were referring to the acceptance meeting or the retrospective report. The post reshapes behaviour: people who mainly maintain systems consolidate first more often, people who mainly work on site reproduce first more often. Worth noting, but not readable backwards into a type.

Put the practice in everyday scenes with a similar role: take three notes you received recently and write four lines for each — what your role was, how tight the deadline was, what material you had (quotations, clauses, reproduction records, logs), and why you took that kind first. Afterwards read the recurring reason across the four lines rather than counting how many times you consolidated or reproduced. These notes serve reflection, are not scored, do not assign a type, and a few weeks of trend cannot replace the interpretation of an assessment result.
sections.title: ENFJ and ESFP: how to keep observing

items.answer:
In the fictional review, either person could ask what patterns appear across similar reports or check the specific conditions and frequency of the observed issue. Those are two ways to gather information, illustrating S/N. Either person can also consider who is affected, which is consistent with their shared F.

That is emphasis, not a work order. If the client gives only their own words, the contract names the acceptance item, and the fault is intermittent, all three push both people toward the same approach; conversely, whoever knows the product better tends to try it first.
items.question: Given the same client note, what does each attend to?

items.answer:
Because both start with E and differ in whether the outward face is judging or perceiving: the last letter decides whether the dominant falls on Fe or Se, and the judging side changes within the same family's attitudes, Fe against Fi and Ti against Te.

The seats are Ni second in ENFJ and fourth in ESFP, Se third in ENFJ and first in ESFP — offset, not exchanged. Both have F as the third letter, so the Fe/Fi difference cannot be attributed to a change in the T/F letter. Sources label the third process differently; check the convention before comparing versions.
items.question: Why are Ni and Se shared while both judging processes change?

items.answer:
Yes, but by the reason rather than by whether it happens: across comparable situations, do you more often cite the phenomena already seen and the conditions for reproducing them, or the effect on people and how it will be accounted for.

A detailed list whose every item names its source and occurrence conditions shows a habit of speaking from checkable material; a clearly categorised list whose every item points back to the client's words or a contract clause shows a habit of building an accountable structure. Both lists may come from the same person, or from two people of the same type, so they are discussion material, not a basis for typing.
items.question: An ESFP also draws up the fix list in advance, an ENFJ also tries the product on the spot — can they still be told apart?

items.answer:
Not a division by type; either can complete the whole process.

If a split is needed, use familiarity with the product, responsibility for client communication, current workload and past work samples: whoever knows the system better reproduces first, whoever deals with clients more often negotiates the order. Taking the same fictional note sheet and writing a reproduction record and a fix schedule separately is a way to feel the difference between the two tasks, not to judge who is competent.
items.question: Which is better suited to acceptance delivery or customer success?

items.answer:
Usually on what the client is actually unhappy about: one records the phenomenon, the other records the attitude, and afterwards they do not match.

A workable agreement writes two lines for each note — one for the reproducible phenomenon and its conditions, one for the exact words used; if neither can be written, do not change anything yet, go and ask. A third line for the source of the evidence, filled with a contract clause, ticket number or chat record, saves arguing later about who misremembered.
items.question: Where do they most often get stuck when delivering together?

items.answer:
Check the assessment name, version, language and scoring guide first. If it reports comparable scores and explains the cutoffs, check whether S/N or J/P was close to its cutoff on either occasion.

Think about the circumstances you had in mind when you answered. Differences in those circumstances may affect your answers, but the two results alone cannot establish the cause. Use similar conditions if you want to compare results, and keep personal notes for reflection.

These links supply the framework and the preference definitions; they do not endorse any behavioural inference in the scenes here.

Four-position convention on this page: the arrangement Fe–Ni–Se–Ti and Se–Fi–Te–Ni, in particular the attitude of the third process, follows a common writing adopted here as an editorial convention; other sources handle it differently, and this page does not present the writing as the Foundation's only reading.

Editorial fiction note: the acceptance meeting, the demo failure and the childcare half day are all editorial fiction, corresponding to no real client, project or person, written to illustrate how people can weigh the same information, and constituting no professional advice.

Scope limits: assessment results are not for ranking ability, hiring screens or predicting relationships; this page does not infer competence from type, nor judge who is better at caring for a child. Anything involving mains power, venue equipment or on-site safety follows site rules and the venue operator's instructions.
